metadata.title: Pass 3 developmental reference: CIN/TCP maturation front, auxin/PIN1 up-the-gradient transport and CUC2 margin patterning coupled to non-Euclidean edge buckling
metadata.provenance_note: Phenotype entries are ORDINAL / qualitative transcriptions of the cited papers made offline (no DOI re-verification in this pass). Numeric serration-count ranges are deliberately broad plausibility bounds, NOT digitised measurements; see README.md Pass 3 addendum.

governing_equations.auxin_pin1_up_the_gradient: da/dt = D_a d2a/dy2 - div J_PIN + rho_a - mu_a a - (dGamma_mar/dt)/(1+Gamma_mar) a;  J_{i->j} = T p_i a_i exp(kappa a_j) / sum_k exp(kappa a_k);  p_i = p_max c_i/(c_half + c_i)
governing_equations.tcp_maturation_front: m(y,t) = 1 / (1 + exp(-(v_tcp t - (L(t) - y)) / w_front))  (basipetal, tip -> base)
governing_equations.growth_strains: dGamma_int/dt = gamma_0 (1 - m);  dGamma_mar/dt = gamma_0 (1 - m)(1 + beta a / a_ref)
governing_equations.excess_metric_to_fvk: g_0(y,t) = ((1 + Gamma_mar)/(1 + Gamma_int))^2 - 1;  g_yy(x,y) = 1 + g_0(y,t) exp(-x/ell)

wild_type_calibration.target_source: Lactuca sativa 'Lollo Bionda' edge excess g_0 used by the Pass 2 mechanical module (ripping_leaf_edge_waves_reference.json default_parameters.g0_edge_excess)
wild_type_calibration.note: gamma_0 and beta_auxin were tuned so the wild-type developmental run lands near this value; this is a self-consistency calibration between the two modules, not an independent measurement.

genotype_phenotype_table.organism_context: Lactuca sativa cv. 'Lollo Bionda' (dissected, ruffled margin); Arabidopsis thaliana Col-0 (serrated margin)
genotype_phenotype_table.margin_phenotype_obs: serrated / lobed margin with primary lobes and smaller secondary serrations; ruffled (K < 0) edge
genotype_phenotype_table.source: Sharon et al. (2002) Nature Fig. 1c; Bilsborough et al. (2011) PNAS Fig. 1; Nath et al. (2003) Science Fig. 1

genotype_phenotype_table.organism_context: Antirrhinum majus cincinnata (cin) mutant; Arabidopsis jaw-D (miR319 over-expression, TCP2/3/4/10/24 down)
genotype_phenotype_table.margin_phenotype_obs: larger, crinkled leaves; delayed/slowed basipetal cell-cycle arrest front; excess marginal growth; negative Gaussian curvature
genotype_phenotype_table.relative_marginal_growth_obs_note: ordinal: > 1 (cin leaves larger with excess margin growth); 1.5 is a placeholder magnitude, not a digitised value
genotype_phenotype_table.source: Nath, Crawford, Carpenter & Coen (2003) Science 299:1404-1407 Fig. 1-3; Palatnik et al. (2003) Nature 425:257-263 Fig. 1

genotype_phenotype_table.organism_context: Arabidopsis 35S::mTCP4 / rTCP (miR319-resistant TCP) and TCP gain-of-function lines
genotype_phenotype_table.margin_phenotype_obs: smaller leaves, precocious differentiation, flatter / less dissected margin
genotype_phenotype_table.source: Palatnik et al. (2003) Nature 425:257-263; Efroni, Blum, Goldshmidt & Eshed (2008) Plant Cell 20:2293-2306; Koyama et al. (2007) Plant Cell 19:473-484

genotype_phenotype_table.margin_phenotype_obs: smooth (unserrated) leaf margin; no PIN1 convergence points / auxin maxima at the margin
genotype_phenotype_table.source: Nikovics et al. (2006) Plant Cell 18:2929-2945; Bilsborough et al. (2011) PNAS 108:3424-3429 Fig. 1-2

genotype_phenotype_table.margin_phenotype_obs: smooth leaf margin; serrations require PIN1-mediated auxin convergence
genotype_phenotype_table.source: Hay, Barkoulas & Tsiantis (2006) Nature Genetics 38:942-947; Bilsborough et al. (2011) PNAS 108:3424-3429

model_predictions_documented.serration_hierarchy_mechanism: new auxin maxima insert between older ones as the Lagrangian margin lattice stretches (Bilsborough et al. 2011 growing-domain mechanism); older maxima accumulate more outgrowth -> primary lobes, later ones -> secondary serrations
model_predictions_documented.basipetal_size_gradient: the TCP arrest front reaches the leaf base last, so basal serrations/lobes accumulate the most outgrowth and the largest excess metric g_0(y)
model_predictions_documented.fvk_coupling: the quasi-static Föppl-von Kármán cascade (relax_foppl_von_karman_cascade) is re-solved on the developmental <g_0(y,t)>; the out-of-plane amplitude is modulated along the margin by sqrt(g_0(y)/<g_0>) (Law 1)
